task.body:
## Problem
`executive_summary` (`runtime/executive/summarizer.py`) always writes `"{n} have blockers and {m} need owner attention."`. With subsystems `[{"id": "a", "name": "A", "status": "healthy"}, {"id": "b", "name": "B", "status": "blocked", "owner_required": True}]` and no priorities, the sentence is `"1/2 executive subsystems are healthy. 1 have blockers and 1 need owner attention."`.

## Required behaviour
- A count of exactly 1 uses the singular verb: `has blockers`, `needs owner attention`; every other count keeps `have` / `need`.
- The example above -> `"1/2 executive subsystems are healthy. 1 has blockers and 1 needs owner attention."`.
- Three blocked subsystems of which two are owner-required -> `"0/3 executive subsystems are healthy. 3 have blockers and 2 need owner attention."` (unchanged).
- Empty input `{"subsystems": [], "priorities": []}` -> `"0/0 executive subsystems are healthy. 0 have blockers and 0 need owner attention."` (unchanged). Every other key of the result is unchanged. Nothing else changes.

## Scope
Allowed paths:
- `runtime/executive/summarizer.py`
- `tests/test_executive_summary_pluralization.py`

Do not change any other file. Existing tests must keep passing unchanged; add new tests only to the test file above. `tests/test_executive_summary_pluralization.py` is a new file.

## Validation
- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_executive_summary_pluralization.py tests/test_build_052_executive_engine.py tests/test_mission_control_regression_001.py`
- `python -m ruff check runtime/executive/summarizer.py tests/test_executive_summary_pluralization.py`

New tests must cover:
- the three inputs above, asserting the exact `executive_summary` sentence.
